subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos(2 Tan⁻¹(1/7)) = sin(2 Tan⁻¹(3/4)).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.74 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 78.1. Printed appearances: AP 18. Nothing is transformed from one side into the other here. Each side is evaluated INDEPENDENTLY, and the proof is that both land on the same number — 24/25. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). The same shape as Unit 7. Verified by walking to p.75, where SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles begins.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Evaluate the left side
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Name the inner inverse as α, so the left side is cos2α — then use the tangent form of cos2α, which is the one that takes tanα directly.
steps.memory_tip: Name the inner inverse α, then use the TANGENT form of cos 2α — it needs no cosα.

recall.must_convey: That the left side is cos2α with tanα = 1/7, evaluated by (1 − tan²α)/(1 + tan²α) to give 24/25.
accept: name tan inverse one seventh as alpha then cos two alpha is one minus tan squared over one plus tan squared giving twenty four over twenty five
the left side evaluates to twenty four twenty fifths
use the tangent form of cos two alpha
cos two alpha ki tan form vaadi twenty four by twenty five vasthundi
the left hand side is twenty four over twenty five

steps.why: cos2θ has three forms, and the tangent one is chosen because tanα is what the inverse hands you directly — no square roots needed.
common_mistakes: Using cos2θ = 2cos²θ − 1 and having to find cosα first.

steps.label: Evaluate the right side
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The right side is sin2β, so use the tangent form of sin2β — 2tanβ/(1+tan²β).
steps.memory_tip: sin 2β = 2tanβ/(1 + tan²β), the tangent form again — no need for sinβ and cosβ.

recall.must_convey: That the right side is sin2β with tanβ = 3/4, evaluated by 2tanβ/(1+tan²β) to give 24/25.
accept: the right side is sin two beta which is two tan beta over one plus tan squared beta giving twenty four over twenty five
evaluate the right hand side to twenty four twenty fifths
use the tangent form of sin two beta
sin two beta ki tan form vaadi twenty four by twenty five vasthundi
the right hand side is also twenty four over twenty five

steps.why: Both sin2θ and cos2θ have tangent forms, which is why this question can be done entirely without finding a single sine or cosine.
common_mistakes: Using sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ and having to find both ratios.
Inverting the fraction at the end.

steps.label: Compare the two sides
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both sides came to 24/25 independently, so they are equal. Say so — a proof by evaluation is not finished until the comparison is stated.
steps.memory_tip: Both sides come to 24/25 independently. A proof by evaluation is not finished until you say so.

recall.must_convey: That results (1) and (2) are both 24/25, so the two sides are equal.
accept: both sides come to twenty four over twenty five so they are equal
from one and two the two sides agree
since both equal the same number the result is proved
rendu sides twenty four by twenty five, so equal
the two sides match so it is proved

steps.why: Evaluating two things is not a proof until you say they agree. That sentence is what the last mark is for.
common_mistakes: Computing both sides and never stating they are equal.

insider_note: Both sides are double angles, so use cos2A = (1 − tan²A)/(1 + tan²A) and sin2A = 2tanA/(1 + tan²A) — no square roots are needed anywhere. Both sides come to 24/25.
